method: Each character is looked up in the GSM 7-bit default alphabet of 3GPP TS 23.038, one septet per character, except the ten extension characters (form feed, ^ { } \ [ ~ ] | and the euro sign), which travel as the escape septet 0x1B plus an extension code and therefore cost two septets; a character outside both tables is refused with its position rather than replaced. The septets are packed seven bits at a time into octets, the first septet in the low bits of the first octet; when exactly seven bits are left spare in the last octet they carry the code of carriage return, because seven zero bits would read back as an @, and the septet count excludes that filler. One message part holds 160 septets in 140 octets; beyond that the text is split into parts of 153 septets, the payload left after a six-octet concatenation header. Reading hex back takes the septet count from the octet length, the largest number of septets that fits, and drops a trailing carriage return only when that derived count exactly fills the octets, since the length alone cannot tell the filler from a typed carriage return; an explicit septet count overrides both rules. Extension codes with no character and data ending on an escape septet are refused. Packed data is limited to 280 octets and text to 1,000 characters. Nothing is uploaded, stored or sent.
